title: Arrays
summary: An array is a row of values of one type, side by side in memory, indexed from 0. C never checks the index, so going past the end is a silent bug. sizeof gives an array's length only where it was declared; a function receives just the address, so pass the length too. Two-dimensional arrays are arrays of rows.

cards.q: What is the last valid index of int a[8]?
What happens when a program writes to a[20] in int a[8]?
cards.a:
It overwrites some other memory: anything can happen

C does not check indexes.

cards.q: Why does a function taking an array also need its length?
cards.a:
It only receives the address of the first element

Pass the count as a separate parameter.

cards.q: int a[10] = {0}; - what are the values?
cards.a:
All ten are 0

Missing initialisers are filled with 0.
